title: Security & Compliance Integrated Playbook: RBAC, Audit Logging, Data Residency & Retention, Secure SDLC, Incident Response, Evidence Workflows & Risk Exceptions
author: Evelyn Chen
summary: Consolidated playbook that standardizes RBAC and authentication controls, centralized audit logging, data residency & retention policies, secure SDLC requirements, incident response security procedures, evidence collection for audits, and the process for granting and tracking risk exceptions.
body:
Overview

This playbook consolidates Redwood Inference security and compliance controls relevant to: RBAC & authentication, centralized audit logging, data residency & retention, secure SDLC gates, incident-response security procedures, evidence collection for audits, and risk/exception workflows. The goal is to provide operational guidance, owner(s), measurable thresholds, and concrete procedures.

Scope
- Applies to all Redwood-managed cloud services (hosted API, Dedicated control plane, Private deployments) and associated operational tooling (console, telemetry pipelines, CI/CD, artifact registries).
- Excludes customer-managed on-prem components that run under a customer SLA unless explicitly contracted.

Primary owners and stakeholders
- Security (owner): Evelyn Chen (security lead)
- Eng-SRE: Capacity & alerting integration
- Eng-Infra: Identity & network enforcement
- Eng-Platform: Telemetry, dashboards, evidence exports
- Product & Legal: Compliance requirements, customer obligations

1) RBAC & Authentication
Purpose: Ensure least-privilege access across control planes, consoles, and infrastructure with auditable role assignments.

Role model (high level):
| Role | Typical membership | Privileges | Approval required |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| admin | Security engineering leads | Full control: role mgmt, infra, billing | Exec or security approval |
| platform-operator | Platform engineers | Deployments, runtime configs, logs | Team lead |
| srep-oncall | SRE rotation | Runbooks, incident commands, limited config | Onboard checklist |
| read-only | Broad engineering audience | Read-only dashboards/metrics | Self-service |

RBAC rules and enforcement:
- All human accounts use SSO (Okta) with enforced MFA (hardware or TOTP).
- Service principals (non-human) must be short-lived where supported (OIDC tokens / AWS STS) or have machine identity bound to KMS.
- Privileged roles must be assigned through the centralized IAM service (IAM UI or infra-as-code PR). Manual assignments are not permitted except via documented exception.
- Role bindings are reviewed quarterly by role owners; review evidence is stored in the compliance evidence bucket.

Onboarding / offboarding checklist (numbered):
1. New hire requests access via HR-to-Okta provisioning flow.
2. Requester selects minimal role(s).
3. Team lead approves in Workday/HR system.
4. Security reviews privileged role requests (if any) within 2 business days.
5. Access expires after 90 days if no activity; re-approval required.

2) Audit Logging
Objective: Centralize security and access logs with immutability, retention, and searchable indexing for investigations and compliance.

Log sources (examples):
- Control plane (console/API) access and admin operations
- Serving runtime: model load/unload, config changes, autoscale events
- Infrastructure: IAM events, VPC changes, key management ops
- CI/CD: deployment approvals, artifact provenance
- Detection: IDS/IPS and WAF alerts

Minimum audit log schema (fields):
- timestamp
- service_name
- region
- principal_id (okta:user:<id> or svc:<name>)
- principal_type (human|service)
- action (e.g., login, create-role, update-config)
- resource (e.g., /api/v1/models/12345)
- outcome (success|failure)
- source_ip
- request_id
- correlation_id
- additional_metadata (stringified JSON)

Logging SLOs and guarantees:
- Control plane events: ingested to central logging pipeline within 30s, searchable in ELK within 5 minutes.
- Critical security events (auth failures, privileged role changes): high-priority alert route to security oncall with P1 SLA.

Immutability and retention:
- Primary logs are written to an append-only object store with WORM-enabled buckets for retention windows.
- Digest snapshots (SHA256) are taken daily and stored separately for tamper detection.

Access to logs:
- Access to raw logs restricted to security and platform-operator roles by default.
- Investigations use redaction tooling and timeboxed access; all access is recorded in a log-access audit ledger.

3) Data Residency and Retention
Policy summary:
- Customer data must reside in the geographic region(s) specified by the customer contract. Supported regions: us-west-2, us-east-1, eu-west-1, ap-southeast-1.
- Retention default: 90 days for request-level telemetry (non-persistent); 7 years for compliance evidence and audit artifacts where required by law/contract.

Retention table (examples):
| Data type | Default retention | Owner | Rationale |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| API request logs (non-sensitive) | 90 days | Eng-Platform | Cost/ops needs |
| Control plane admin audit | 7 years | Security | Compliance/legal |
| Telemetry traces (high-cardinality) | 30 days | Eng-SRE | Performance debugging |
| Embeddings, model outputs (customer-managed) | Per customer contract | Customer | Data subject control |

Data residency controls:
- Deployment manifests include region tags; runtime enforces region-based routing with strict egress controls.
- Backups and snapshot exports respect residency: no automatic cross-region replication unless explicitly enabled and contracted.

Data deletion and disposition:
- Deletion requests are implemented via an automated job with an immutable manifest and verification.
- For PII or regulated customer data, deletion is subject to the customer's retention policy; deletion operations produce a signed proof-of-deletion artifact stored in evidence archive.

4) Secure SDLC Requirements
Gates and checks integrated into CI/CD pipeline:
- Static analysis (SAST) and dependency scan mandatory for all repositories.
- Secrets scanning on every PR and pre-merge.
- Pull requests that change IAM policies, runtime kernels, or network rules require security review and a second engineering approver.
- Model onboarding requires a security & privacy checklist: data provenance, license compatibility, quantization impact assessment, and performance regression baseline.

Release checklist (minimum):
1. All PRs pass CI with 0 high-severity SAST findings.
2. Security reviewer sign-off for infra or privileged changes.
3. Canary rollout plan and automatic rollback thresholds defined.
4. Observability hooks present (traces, metrics, logs).

5) Incident Response (Security Procedures)
Purpose: Provide clear steps for detection, containment, eradication, recovery, and post-incident evidence handling.

Severity levels:
- Sev1 (P1): Active data exfiltration, production control-plane compromise, customer-impacting service outage >30 minutes.
- Sev2 (P2): Privilege escalation attempt, successful but contained intrusion, partial service degradation.
- Sev3 (P3): Anomalous activity with low impact.

Incident response run (numbered):
1. Detection & Triage: Oncall or automated detector creates an incident in the tracking system and assigns severity within 15 minutes.
2. Containment: Apply short-term controls (revoke tokens, rotate keys, isolate hosts).
3. Investigation: Collect immutable evidence (WORM logs, disk snapshots), capture timeline, preserve volatile memory when needed.
4. Eradication & Recovery: Remove artifacts, patch, restore from known-good images, validate via integration tests.
5. Notification: Notify impacted customers per contractual obligations and legal requirements.
6. Postmortem: Complete RCA, timeline, mitigations, and update runbooks within 7 business days for P1 incidents.

Evidence handling during incidents:
- Evidence artifacts must be stored in a designated secure evidence bucket with restricted access and retention of 7 years for P1 events.
- Chain-of-custody is recorded as a simple ledger entry (timestamp, actor, artifact-id, reason, hashes).

6) Compliance Evidence Workflows
Standard artifacts we produce for audits:
- Role assignment exports and quarterly review logs
- Immutable audit-log export covering the scope period
- SOC/ISO/PCI artifacts (attestations, controls mapping) as applicable
- Secure SDLC records: SAST reports, dependency scans, review approvals
- Incident timelines and evidence collection manifests

Evidence generation process (brief):
- Evidence requests submitted through the compliance portal (internal ticketing).
- Owner (security) validates scope and produces export within SLA (standard: 5 business days for internal audits, 10 for external auditors; expedited available by approval).
- All exports are accompanied by a verification manifest (hashes, signature) and stored in the evidence archive bucket.

7) Risk & Exceptions
Exception policy:
- Exceptions are allowed only when compensating controls mitigate the residual risk and a written justification is approved by security and the relevant business owner.
- Exceptions expire automatically and must include a mitigation plan and re-evaluation schedule.

Exception process (numbered):
1. Submit exception request with rationale, affected systems, compensating controls, and target expiration.
2. Security reviews and assigns a residual risk rating (Low/Medium/High).
3. Business owner approves; security grants conditional exception with mitigation commitments.
4. Tracking: All exceptions tracked in central register with quarterly review.

Risk assessment template (fields in request form):
- risk_summary
- affected_assets
- likelihood (Low|Medium|High)
- impact (Low|Medium|High)
- compensating_controls
- expiration_date

Operational metrics and review cadence
- Quarterly audits of role bindings and evidence completeness.
- Monthly review of retention buckets and cross-region replications.
- Post-incident tracking: % of P1 postmortems completed within SLA (target 100%), average time to evidence delivery for audits (target <=5 business days).

Appendices
A. Example audit query: retrieve all admin role grants in last 90 days
- ELK query: service_name:control_plane AND action:create-role AND role:admin AND timestamp:[now-90d TO now]

B. Sample audit log JSON (single event)
{
  "timestamp": "2026-09-30T15:22:10Z",
  "service_name": "control_plane",
  "principal_id": "okta:user:U12345",
  "principal_type": "human",
  "action": "update-role",
  "resource": "/roles/admin",
  "outcome": "success",
  "request_id": "req-8f7a9b"
}
